words-only.why: I checked each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions against its expect line. Checks 1, 2 and 4 only test values and behaviour that their lines require. Check 3 breaks the criterion. Its PASS condition needs `missing: none` from a regex, `'^#+\\s*'+f+'\\b'`, that only matches a heading starting with the function's name. "A section for every function" doesn't require that heading format. The regex is also broken: bash double quotes turn `\\s` into `\s` and `\\b` into `\b`, and in a JS string those become a literal "s" and a backspace character. So even `## padLeft(s, width, fill)` would not match, and Check 3 would fail a README that meets the line. That makes the PASS condition stricter than the words, and it isn't under Advisory.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs. `npm test` exists in package.json, and the Check 1 and Check 2 one-liners are valid and fit `node --input-type=module -e`. Check 3 is broken by its quoting. The JavaScript sits inside a bash double-quoted string, so the shell turns `'^#+\\s*'` and `'\\b'` into `'^#+\s*'` and `'\b'`. JavaScript then reads `'\s'` as just `s` and `'\b'` as a backspace character. The regex that gets built is `^#+s*capitalize<backspace>`, which never matches a heading like `## capitalize(s)`. So the command would always print every export as missing. Its PASS output, `missing: none`, can never appear, even when the README is correct. Run as written, that command doesn't work in this repository, so the criterion fails.

catches-traps.why:
I checked all three must_catch items, and the briefs handle each one.

1. Builder step 2 says "ALSO add the missing `## slugify(s)` section" next to the padLeft section. It also requires a heading for "capitalize, slugify, truncate and padLeft".

2. Verifier Check 3 prints index.js's exports and any missing ones. PASS needs "at least capitalize, slugify, truncate, padLeft" to each have a heading. FAIL covers "any exported function, including slugify, has no README section". It also notes that slugify had no section before the change.

3. Verifier Check 1 calls `m.padLeft('42',5)` with no fill argument. It expects `"   42"` in the output, so it checks that padding uses spaces.

avoids-must-not.why:
Must_not 1 holds: Check 3 fails explicitly when slugify has no section ("FAIL: any exported function, including slugify, has no README section").

Must_not 2 breaks. Check 3's PASS needs the script to print `missing: none`, and the script requires a heading of the form `^#+\s*name\b`. That is a README layout rule. A section with a heading like "### `padLeft(...)`" would fail it. The regex is also broken as written. Inside bash double quotes, `\\s` and `\\b` turn into `\s` and `\b` in the JS string, which become a literal "s" and a backspace character. So the pattern never matches, and every function is reported missing even when the README is correct. In practice the PASS condition is stricter than "README.md has a section for every function". Checks 1, 2 and 4 match their lines and have no extra conditions such as a single-character fill or a parameter count.

methods-private.why: I compared the builder brief's concrete examples with the verifier's probes. Verifier Check 1 runs padLeft('42',5,'0') and padLeft('42',5) and expects `00042` and `"   42"`. The builder brief uses the same inputs and outputs twice: in step 1 ("`padLeft('42', 5, '0')` returns `'00042'`, and `padLeft('42', 5)` returns `'   42'`") and in step 3 ("('42', 5, '0') -> '00042'; default space fill ('42', 5) -> '   42'"). The brief is allowed to tell the builder to write its own tests, but here it hands over the verifier's exact input/expected-output pairs, so those probes leak to the builder. Step 2's "README.md must have a `##` section heading for every function... capitalize, slugify, truncate and padLeft" also mirrors Check 3's PASS condition. Because of the shared inputs and outputs, the criterion is not met.
